# Romance lens

Apply when a central romantic relationship or its development is a primary narrative engine. For romantic subplots, use only the relevant prompts.

## Chapter-level prompts

- Track each partner's stated goals, private needs only when text supports them, fears, boundaries, and current understanding of the relationship.
- Record relationship state at chapter end: first contact, growing trust, attraction, conflict, rupture, repair, commitment, or another text-supported phase. Do not force a fixed beat sequence.
- Identify emotional turning points and their causes: a choice, disclosure, misunderstanding, act of care, betrayal, external pressure, or change in self-understanding.
- Distinguish external obstacles (social, familial, practical, antagonistic) from internal obstacles (fear, values, assumptions); note who has agency and what each risks.
- Track consent, communication, power differences, and boundary-respecting or boundary-crossing behavior factually and without excusing harmful conduct as inherently romantic.
- Explain how dialogue, subtext, proximity, gesture, point of view, and pacing build or complicate intimacy.

## Whole-work prompts

- Trace how both partners change individually and together; assess reciprocity, compatibility, conflict repair, and whether the resolution is supported by their demonstrated choices.
- Identify relationship milestones and their setup/payoff by chapter. Consider whether the central conflict is resolved through character agency or merely disappears.
- If the book promises a happily-ever-after or happy-for-now ending, assess whether the ending meets that narrative promise; do not impose that convention on works that make no such promise.
- For romantic suspense or fantasy romance, combine this lens with the relevant mystery/speculative lens rather than letting romance obscure the external plot's causal logic.

## Guardrails

- Do not infer attraction, consent, or a relationship label without textual support.
- Do not reduce characters to a couple; retain independent goals, friendships, and arcs.
- Do not treat jealousy, coercion, or abuse as proof of love. Describe behavior and narrative framing precisely.
